data.title: Names are not type safety (2020)
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Haskell中实现类型安全的两类方法：构造性数据建模与`newtype`包装。构造性数据建模通过定义明确的类型和构造函数来确保非法状态不可表示，例如用枚举类型表示1到5的整数。这种方法使编译器能够进行穷尽性检查，从而提供强类型安全。相对的，`newtype`只是对现有类型的包装，虽然可以通过智能构造函数进行验证，但不能在编译时保证穷尽性检查。这意味着使用`newtype`时，下游函数可能需要处理非法状态，从而削弱了类型安全性。文章强调，名字（即`newtype`）本身并不等同于类型安全，构造性建模提供了更强的安全保障。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中的新类型（newtype）的使用及其在类型安全和类型系统中的作用

不同观点：
• **支持新类型的观点**：
  - [nixpulvers] 认为新类型通过实现 `Deref` 可以提供良好的类型安全，防止将错误的类型传递给函数（如将用户UUID误作帖子UUID传递）。
  - [5pl1n73r] 指出新类型的主要目的是解决类型类问题，并且它们被设计为零成本。通过不导出数据构造器，可以实现抽象数据类型，无论是否使用新类型。
  
• **质疑新类型必要性的观点**：
  - [lmm] 认为类型安全主要来自于命名，而不是新类型。类型检查可以通过命名轻松绕过，而大多数编程中的类型关系是业务关系，难以用形式化表达。
  - [auggierose] 认为这些类型是浪费时间，认为像 `OneToSix` 或 `OneToSeven` 这样的类型没有实际意义。
  - [b_e_n_t_o_n] 表示不理解将这种逻辑编码进类型系统的必要性，认为像Go一样使用结构体和方法已经足够。

• **关于类型范围和编译时检查的观点**：
  - [skybrian] 认为编译时范围检查在实际应用中可能不合理，特别是在动态内存分配时，限制应在系统边界设置。
  - [kazinator] 提出是否可以扩展新类型以支持子范围类型，例如 `MinusIntMaxToPlusIntMax`，质疑新类型在可枚举类型中的局限性。

• **关于程序正确性和运行时检查的观点**：
  - [andyferris] 认为在很多情况下，运行时检查和崩溃比提供程序正确性证明更实际，通过早期崩溃可以实现足够可靠的软件。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于新类型是否真正提供了足够的类型安全，还是仅仅增加了不必要的复杂性。
- 不同语言（如Haskell和Go）在实现类型安全和抽象数据类型上的不同做法也引发了对新类型实用性的讨论。
- 另一个值得注意的点是编译时检查的合理性以及类型范围的实际需求。

Haskell programmers spend a lot of time talking about
type safety
. The Haskell school of program construction advocates “capturing invariants in the type system” and “making illegal states unrepresentable,” both of which sound like compelling goals, but are rather vague on the techniques used to achieve them. Almost exactly one year ago, I published
Parse, Don’t Validate
as an initial stab towards bridging that gap.
The ensuing discussions were largely productive and right-minded, but one particular source of confusion quickly became clear: Haskell’s
newtype
construct. The idea is simple enough—the
newtype
keyword declares a wrapper type, nominally distinct from but representationally equivalent to the type it wraps—and on the surface this
sounds
like a simple and straightforward path to type safety. For example, one might consider using a
newtype
declaration to define a type for an email address:
newtype
EmailAddress
=
EmailAddress
Text
This technique can provide
some
value, and when coupled with a smart constructor and an encapsulation boundary, it can even provide some safety. But it is a meaningfully distinct
kind
of type safety from the one I highlighted a year ago, one that is far weaker. On its own, a newtype is just a name.
And names are not type safety.

To illustrate the difference between constructive data modeling (discussed at length in my
previous blog post
) and newtype wrappers, let’s consider an example. Suppose we want a type for “an integer between 1 and 5, inclusive.” The natural constructive modeling would be an enumeration with five cases:

data.title: So you want to parse a PDF?
data.author: UglyToad
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了如何解析PDF文件，强调了实际操作中的困难。理想情况下，解析PDF包括以下步骤：找到文件头、定位交叉引用表指针、查找所有对象偏移量、构建尾部字典并找到目录字典。PDF文件是由多个对象组成的图形结构，对象之间通过间接引用相互连接。为了避免扫描整个文件，PDF使用交叉引用表（xref）来索引对象位置，文件末尾有指向该表的指针。然而，实际情况中，文件常有不规范的情况，如指针位置错误、拼写错误或格式异常，甚至有约0.5%的文件存在错误的xref声明。此外，有些文件在非零偏移处开始内容，可能包含垃圾数据，进一步增加了解析难度。因此，解析PDF常常面临诸多挑战，被形容为“PDF地狱”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PDF解析的复杂性及其实际应用中的问题

不同观点：
• **依赖元数据 vs. 依赖计算机视觉**：
  - [gcanyon] 认为应在PDF中附加统一的元数据，以便机器解析，避免文本解析错误，例如名字 "Geo" 和 "ff" 被分开识别的问题。
  - [diptanu] 反驳称，依赖元数据不现实，因为不同来源的PDF差异很大。其公司采用计算机视觉和布局识别技术来处理PDF解析问题，这样才能在实际应用中获得较好的结果。

• **PDF解析的技术难点**：
  - [farkin88] 指出，在多应用编辑后的PDF中，startxref偏移量可能不准确，许多PDF查看器会通过暴力扫描来修复文档，而严格的解析器则可能失败。
  - [JKCalhoun] 提到，PDF格式设计之初未考虑流媒体需求，必须等到文件完全加载才能解析，尽管有些PDF可以通过一些技巧实现首页的提前渲染。

• **PDF格式的复杂演变**：
  - [userbinator] 强调，PDF格式非常复杂，尤其是1.5版后引入的xref流和对象流，使得解析更加困难。
  - [HocusLocus] 进一步分析了PDF的底层结构，如ASCII、Flate/ZIP、LZW、RLE压缩等，指出深度解析和处理这些文件是一个痛苦的过程。

补充讨论：
• **实际应用中的失败案例**：
  - [wackget] 明确表示不愿意解析PDF，因其格式带来的种种问题。
  - [yoyohello13] 分享了自己尝试解析PDF失败的经历，表明即使是简单的自动化任务也难以完成。

• **替代方案和工具**：
  - [pss314] 推荐使用pdfgrep工具来搜索PDF文本，作为命令行下的实用解决方案。
  - [simonw] 建议将PDF转换为图像，然后使用OCR或视觉LLM处理，尤其是面对复杂布局时。
  - [ccgreg] 提供了一个包含8百万PDF文件的数据集链接，供研究和开发使用。

• **用户体验和格式选择**：
  - [anon-3988] 抱怨在处理多语言PDF时遇到的困难，提议使用Markdown等更简单的文本格式来替代PDF，以获得更好的可读性和处理体验。

争议焦点：
- **元数据与视觉识别的优劣**：一方认为统一元数据是解决PDF解析问题的关键，另一方则认为现实中元数据不可靠，计算机视觉和布局识别才是更有效的解决方案。
- **PDF格式的复杂性**：用户对PDF格式演变带来的技术挑战感到困扰，尤其是不同版本间的差异和解析器的兼容性问题。

44780353.article_content:
So you want to parse a PDF?
03 Aug, 2025
Suppose you have an appetite for tilting at windmills. Let's say you love pain. Well then why not write a PDF parser today?
The ideal world: how the specification should work
Conceptually parsing a PDF is fairly simple:
First, locate the version header comment at the start of the file
Next you need to locate the pointer to the cross-reference
Then you can find all object offsets
Finally you locate and build the trailer dictionary which points to the catalog dicitionary
Introduction to PDF objects
A PDF object wraps some valid PDF content, numbers, strings, dictionaries, etc., in an object and generation number. The content is surrounded by the
obj/endobj
markers, for example a simple number may have its own PDF object:
16 0 obj
620
endobj
This declares that object 16 with generation 0 contains the number 620.
A PDF file is effectively a graph of objects that may reference each other. Objects reference other objects by use of indirect references. These have the format "16 0 R" which indicates that the content
should be found in object 16 (generation number 0). In this case that would point to the object 16 containing the number 620. It is up to producer applications to split file content into objects as they wish, though the specification requires that certain object types be indirect.
Finding the cross-reference offset
To avoid the need to scan the entire file, PDFs declare a cross-reference table (xref). This is an index pointing to where each object in the file lives.
Each file ends with a pointer to the cross-reference file:
<< %trailer >>
startxref
116
%%EOF
This tells the parser to jump to byte offset 116 to find the xref table (or stream). In theory this pointer is right at the end of the file, according to the specification:
Applications should read a PDF file from its end. The last line of the file contains only the end-of-file marker,
%%EOF
Though the specification says the
%%EOF
marker should be on the last line, in practice, things are much messier. For example, Adobe Acrobat only requires it to be within the last 1024 bytes. In real files it can appear anywhere.
In addition files encountered in the wild lacked a linebreak before the offset declaration, or had a typo, e.g.
startref
.
Let's assume you're able to find the declared cross-reference offset for now.
Finding all object offsets
At the specified offset you should find a well-formatted xref table:
xref
7 4
0000000000 65535 f
0000109882 00000 n
0000109933 00000 n
0000140066 00000 n
After the
xref
indicator appears, followed by a line break, the first object number and count of objects in the subsection are given. This means: start at object 7 and list 4 objects. Each line gives the byte offset, generation number, and status (n for in-use, f for free). From this, we know where to find objects 8-10 in the file.
So in the example above -- skipping the free entry for object 7 -- this xref table tells where to find the following objects:
Object 8 (generation 0) at offset 109882
Object 9 (generation 0) at offset 109933
Object 10 (generation 0) at offset 140066
Note: files can have multiple xref tables or streams, linked by
/Prev
entries in their trailers.
Locating the trailer dictionary
Finally, above the startxref marker, you'll find the trailer dictionary. This provides key metadata, most importantly, where to find the root object. Once you have that, you can follow references and begin interpreting the content.
The real world: where your pain begins
Assuming everything is well behaved and you have a reasonable parser for PDF objects this is fairly simple. But you cannot assume everything is well behaved. That would be very foolish, foolish indeed. You're in PDF hell
now. PDF isn't a specification, it's a social construct, it's a vibe. The more you struggle the deeper you sink. You live in the bog now, with the rest of us, far from the sight of God. If your parser expects files to obey the specification it will fail and people will think it is broken and pitiable. They will think that you are very silly.
The challenges of locating the xref pointer
We've already mentioned a few unexpected ways locating the pointer to the first cross-reference can fail:
It is not at the end of the file, nor within the last 1024 bytes of the file.
It is misspelled.
It is not in the format you'd expect.
But assuming you find a pointer, that's where the real fun begins. Because the pointer is not your friend, it is the first lie, you don't appreciate how deep the rabbit hole goes.
In screening 3977 files taken from the
common crawl corpus
at random we detected 23 files with a bad xref declaration. This works out to a roughly 0.5% failure rate in the sample set.
PDF content starting at a non-zero offset
In these files the
startxref
pointer is incorrect due to a non-zero PDF content start.
This happens when there's junk data before the
%PDF-
version header. This shifts every single byte offset in the file.

data.title: A study of lights at night suggests dictators lie about economic growth (2022)
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 文章通过分析夜间灯光卫星数据，揭示独裁国家可能在经济成长数据上造假。尽管自2002年以来，独裁政权的官方GDP增长率声称比民主国家快两倍，但夜间灯光（通常反映经济活动）并未显示出相应增长，暗示这些国家可能夸大了经济表现。文章特别提到，独裁者常被视为高效的领导者，但数据表明其经济成就可能并不真实。

data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图像或声音中识别出具有意义的图案或形状的心理现象，即pareidolia现象。

不同观点：
• 观点一（anilgulecha）：该评论直接引用了"Pareidolia"这一术语，认为人们在这种图像或声音中识别出特定形状或意义是一种pareidolia现象。支持这一观点的例子是维基百科中关于pareidolia的定义，即人类倾向于在随机数据中识别出熟悉的模式，例如在云中看到动物形状，或在噪音中听到话语。

• 观点二：未明确提出反对意见，但潜在的另一种看法可能是质疑这种现象是否真的只是心理学上的解释。例如，有些人可能会认为这些图像或声音中的模式可能具有实际意义或外在原因，而非单纯的心理投射。这种观点的支持者可能会指出某些超自然现象或未解之谜，认为不能简单归结为心理错觉。

补充讨论：
• Pareidolia现象的普遍性：评论中隐含了这种现象在日常生活中非常普遍，几乎每个人都有可能经历过类似的情境。
• 科学解释与主观体验的对立：科学上将pareidolia归结为大脑的模式识别功能过度活跃，而主观体验上，人们可能更倾向于相信自己看到的或听到的具有某种特殊意义。
• 争议焦点：争议的核心在于是否所有此类识别模式的现象都可以用科学解释完全涵盖，还是存在一些未被科学解释的超自然或神秘现象。这涉及到心理学与超自然信仰之间的张力。

data.title: Welcome to url.town, population 465
data.author: plaguna
data.article_summary: MIT开放课程资源提供了免费的在线课程材料，涵盖广泛的学科领域。文章列出了各种资源类别，包括计算机与教育资源、艺术与设计（如动漫、插画、建筑等）、家庭活动、食品与健康、游戏、兴趣爱好、互联网工具、语言、LGBTQ+支持、数学与科学、音乐、自然、新闻、组织与慈善、摄影、播客、阅读与文学、购物以及社交和体育等。每个类别下包含具体的子项，如博客引擎、浏览器扩展、卡牌游戏、植物种植、心理健康、音乐软件、摄影应用等，为用户提供了丰富的学习和娱乐资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个类似Yahoo的复古网站及其功能、设计和商业模式的看法与讨论

不同观点：
• 一些用户对复古网站的复兴表示欢迎，并提出可以进一步发展，例如Waraqa建议创建一个兼容旧浏览器的静态网站社交媒体平台，BobbyTables2则开玩笑地建议添加Web Ring功能。
• 部分用户对网站的商业模式提出质疑，例如poink认为购买omg.lol的URL不值得，并指出这不是针对所有人的产品。blenderob也表达了类似的担忧，不理解为什么需要购买omg.lol的子域名才能贡献链接。
• amiga386通过引用url.city的历史链接，强调这种类型的网站并非全新概念，而是对过去网络形式的复兴。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户对网站的内容分类提出了意见。thefaux指出网站的体育分类下只有公路自行车，过于单一。toyg则对缺乏汽车和摩托车相关内容感到失望，并将此归因于年轻用户兴趣的转变。
• dredmorbius从信息架构的角度，讨论了网站分类系统的稳定性和未来迁移的可能性，提出了信息是否应以层次结构组织的问题。
• 部分用户对技术实现提出看法，veqq称赞了网站登录系统，而pavel_lishin希望网站能显示每个类别的条目数量以提高用户体验。
• 最后，archerx对网站使用的衬线字体表示不满，认为这种设计选择影响阅读体验。

争议焦点：
• 网站的商业模式，特别是购买omg.lol子域名的必要性，引发了部分用户的不满和质疑。
• 网站内容分类的广泛性和代表性也成为讨论的焦点，尤其是对某些兴趣领域的缺失，部分用户表示失望。

总体来看，讨论围绕网站的设计、功能、商业模式及内容分类展开，体现了用户对复古网站的不同期望和需求。

data.author: codydeluisio
data.article_summary: UniFi OS Server是Ubiquiti推出的自托管平台，允许用户在自己的硬件上运行UniFi Network及部分应用程序（如InnerSpace和Identity），无需Dream Machine或Cloud Key。它支持x86、x64和ARM64架构，兼容UXG网关，但不支持Cloud Gateways。该平台引入了环境分析、SD-WAN式组网、Zero Trust访问等新功能，但仍需Ubiquiti登录以使用云功能。当前版本不支持Protect、Talk、Access等应用，且缺乏多租户管理和全局MSP角色分配功能。对于已经自托管UniFi Network的用户，该平台提供了一些实用功能，但并未彻底改变MSP的管理方式，主要是一次后端改进而非前端革新。

44779839.article_content:
August 3, 2025
Cody Deluisio
Everything You Need to Know About UniFi OS Server (Before You Waste Time Testing It)
UniFi OS Server is now available in Early Access, and it’s being promoted as a major advancement for MSPs and enterprise IT teams. But does it actually solve any problems we couldn’t already work around? Let’s break down what this release is, what it isn’t, and whether it brings real benefits to the table.
Table of Contents
What is UniFi OS Server?
UniFi OS Server
is a self-hosted platform that lets you run UniFi Network and select UniFi apps (currently InnerSpace and Identity) on
your own
hardware — no Dream Machine or Cloud Key required.
It’s a containerized stack that mimics what Ubiquiti runs on their own consoles. The idea is simple: let MSPs and advanced users build their own UniFi cloud console, using their choice of hardware.
Summary:
Runs on x86, x64, or ARM64
Supports UniFi Network, InnerSpace, and Identity
Works with UXG Gateways, not Cloud Gateways
No license fees
Still requires Ubiquiti login for cloud features
So… What’s New?
If you’ve been self-hosting UniFi Network for years, UniFi OS Server will feel very familiar. The difference is that it brings support for Ubiquiti’s newer cloud features — things like:
InnerSpace
for environmental/RF analytics
Site Magic
for SD-WAN-style meshing
UniFi Identity
for Zero Trust user and device access
Organization Manager
(future-facing)
Centralized firmware rollouts
Previously, many of these features were exclusive to UniFi Consoles. Now, they’re accessible from your own server — as long as you’re not trying to manage Cloud Gateways, which still require the traditional unifi.ui.com flow.
What You Still Can’t Do
There are limitations you should know about:
No support for Cloud Gateways (UCG, UDM, etc.)
Those still run their own onboard controller. They cannot be adopted into UniFi OS Server.
No centralized org-wide management yet
Identity Hub and Organization Manager are early and not fully fleshed out. There’s no way today to assign global MSP-level staff roles across multiple client orgs.
No support for Protect, Talk, or Access
As of now, these applications are not available in UOS.
No change in licensing model
This is still Ubiquiti — no license costs, but also no clear roadmap or commitment to long-term MSP tooling improvements.
MSP Use Case: Is It Worth It?
Maybe.
If you’re already self-hosting
UniFi Network
, this adds some useful functionality. Site Magic and Identity are helpful. It could reduce your dependency on Dream Machines for small sites and let you consolidate site management on your own gear.
But the core drawbacks remain:
You still need one instance per tenant or client
There’s no multi-tenancy or role-based MSP hierarchy
No direct adoption of UCG/UDM hardware
You still depend on UI cloud services for key features
So if you were hoping this would replace
unifi.ui.com
or give you a real MSP control panel — it doesn’t. Not yet, anyway.
Final Thoughts
UniFi OS Server is a small but useful upgrade for those already managing UniFi at scale.
It’s not revolutionary, and it’s not a game-changer for MSPs — at least not in its current form.
If you want advanced analytics, SD-WAN features, and Identity support without relying on Dream Machines, it’s worth looking into. But for now, expect more of a backend improvement than a front-end transformation.

data.title: Learnable Programming (2012)
data.author: kunzhi
data.article_summary: Bret Victor在《可学习的编程》一文中探讨了如何让人们更好地理解编程。他批评了Khan Academy的JavaScript和Processing教学环境，认为这些工具无法有效支持学习者理解程序执行过程，且依赖于让学习者通过随机调整参数来猜测功能，这并不是真正的学习。Victor提出，编程系统应帮助学习者阅读词汇、跟踪流程、查看状态，并通过反应和抽象进行创造。编程语言应提供身份和隐喻、分解和重组思维的能力，并注重可读性。他强调，编程环境应使意义透明，减少对API细节的记忆负担，让学习者专注于理解编程的核心概念和思维方式，而非机械操作。最终，Victor建议通过改变编程本身，使其成为人们易于理解的事物。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程中的影响以及编程技能的价值

不同观点：
• mettamage认为LLM（如ChatGPT等大型语言模型）现在已经成为主流，他想知道像Bret这样的专家是否有新的看法或更新观点。这暗示了对LLM快速发展的关注以及其对技术领域影响的疑问。

• fluxkernel提出，在LLM驱动的编码助手和代理的时代，编程技能是否仍然重要。他认为，计算机科学与编程的区别在当下显得尤为明显，强调设计和算法思维可能比单纯编程技能更为重要。这暗示了对传统编程技能价值下降的担忧，并建议将重点转移到更高层次的思维能力上。

补充讨论：
• fluxkernel的观点隐含了对技术发展趋势的判断，即LLM可能取代部分传统的编程工作，从而改变编程在计算机科学中的地位。

• 争议的焦点在于编程技能在LLM时代是否仍然重要。mettamage的疑问反映了对专家观点更新的需求，而fluxkernel则直接质疑编程技能在未来技术环境中的核心地位，主张更多关注设计和算法思维。

• 值得注意的是，fluxkernel提到了"计算机科学 != 编程"这一观点，强调了计算机科学作为一个更广泛领域的多维度性质，而不仅仅是编码技能的掌握。这一观点可能引发关于技术教育和技能培训方向的进一步讨论。

44780552.article_content:
Learnable Programming
Designing a programming system for understanding programs
Bret Victor
/ September 2012
Here's a trick question:
How do we get people to understand programming?
Khan Academy recently launched an
online environment
for learning to program.  It offers a set of tutorials based on the JavaScript and Processing languages, and features a "live coding" environment, where the program's output updates as the programmer types.
Because my work was
cited
as an inspiration for the Khan system, I felt I should respond with two thoughts about learning:
Programming is a way of thinking, not a rote skill.
Learning about "for" loops is not learning to program, any more than learning about pencils is learning to draw.
People understand what they can see.
If a programmer cannot see what a program is doing, she can't understand it.
Thus, the goals of a programming system should be:
to support and encourage powerful ways of thinking
to enable programmers to see and understand the execution of their programs
A live-coding Processing environment addresses neither of these goals.  JavaScript and Processing are poorly-designed languages that support weak ways of thinking, and ignore decades of learning about learning.  And live coding, as a standalone feature, misses the point.
Alan Perlis wrote,
"To understand a program, you must become both the machine and the program."
This view is a mistake, and it is this widespread and virulent mistake that keeps programming a difficult and obscure art.  A person is not a machine, and should not be forced to think like one.
How do we get people to understand programming?
We change programming.  We turn it into something that's understandable by people.
Contents
The concept of a system split between the computer and the head was derived from Will Wright's
thoughts on games
.
A programming system has two parts.  The programming "environment" is the part that's installed on the computer.  The programming "language" is the part that's installed in the programmer's head.
This essay presents a set of design principles for an environment and language suitable for learning.
The
environment
should allow the learner to:
read the vocabulary
-- what do these words mean?
follow the flow
-- what happens when?
see the state
-- what is the computer thinking?
create by reacting
-- start somewhere, then sculpt
create by abstracting
-- start concrete, then generalize
The
language
should provide:
identity and metaphor
-- how can I relate the computer's world to my own?
decomposition
-- how do I break down my thoughts into mind-sized pieces?
recomposition
-- how do I glue pieces together?
readability
-- what do these words mean?
The features are not the point
We often think of a programming environment or language in terms of its
features
-- this one "has code folding", that one "has type inference".  This is like thinking about a book in terms of its
words
-- this book has a "fortuitous", that one has a "munificent".  What matters is not individual words, but how the words together convey a
message
.
Likewise, a well-designed system is not simply a bag of features.  A good system is designed to encourage particular
ways of thinking
, with all features carefully and cohesively designed around that purpose.
This essay will present many features!  The trick is to see
through
them -- to see the underlying design principles that they represent, and understand how these principles
enable the programmer to think.
Read the vocabulary
Here is a simple tutorial program that a learner might face:
For the sake of comparison, the examples here will use the same languages as the Khan Academy system, JavaScript and Processing.
Before a reader can make any sense of this code, before she can even
begin
to understand how it works, here are some questions she will have:
What does "fill" mean?
What do those numbers after "fill" mean?
What do those numbers after "ellipse" mean?
What units are these numbers in?  What ranges are they in?
Why are there so many numbers?
Khan Academy's tutorials encourage the learner to address these questions by
randomly adjusting numbers
and trying to figure out what they do.
Thought experiment.  Imagine if you bought a new microwave, took it out of the box, and found a panel of unlabeled buttons.
Imagine if the microwave encouraged you to randomly hit buttons until you figured out what they did.
Now, imagine if your cookbook advised you that randomly hitting unlabeled buttons was
how you learn cooking
.
Make meaning transparent
Learning cooking is not about guessing the functionality of your kitchen appliances.  It's about understanding how ingredients can be combined.
Likewise, guessing the third argument of the "ellipse" function isn't "learning programming".  It's simply a
barrier
to learning.  In a modern environment, memorizing the minutia of an API should be as relevant as memorizing times tables.

• fluxkernel的观点隐含了对技术发展趋势的判断，即LLM可能取代部分传统的编程工作，从而改变编程在计算机科学中的地位。

• 争议的焦点在于编程技能在LLM时代是否仍然重要。mettamage的疑问反映了对专家观点更新的需求，而fluxkernel则直接质疑编程技能在未来技术环境中的核心地位，主张更多关注设计和算法思维。

• 值得注意的是，fluxkernel提到了"计算机科学 != 编程"这一观点，强调了计算机科学作为一个更广泛领域的多维度性质，而不仅仅是编码技能的掌握。这一观点可能引发关于技术教育和技能培训方向的进一步讨论。

data.title: System-Wide Safety Project
data.author: pieterk
data.article_summary: NASA的系统范围安全（SWS）项目旨在通过新的研究工具、创新技术和操作方法，确保航空运输在满足全球需求增长的同时变得更加高效和便捷。项目由Summer Brandt领导，关键成员包括Michael Vincent和Dr. Wendy Okolo。SWS项目关注无人机安全管理系统的进展、驾驶舱 distractions 的缓解策略、协作决策以及航空安全的未来。此外，NASA还研究如何减轻机场周围的风险，并通过视频展示项目活动。项目定期发布新闻通讯，并邀请公众参与和了解更多信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无人机及航空旅行的未来变化

不同观点：
• 一位评论者对航空旅行和空域变化的具体内容感到困惑，不确定这些变化是为了商用交付无人机还是其他用途。该评论者提出问题：这些变化是否仅仅是为了适应无人机的发展，还是无人机将在空域中承担更多其他功能。

data.title: Show HN: Spatial Web Browser Engine
data.author: yorkie
data.article_summary: 《Design for Spatial Web》一文介绍了一个新的网页设计概念，其中每个HTML元素都可以通过JSAR技术在浏览器中进行空间渲染。这意味着网页元素不再局限于二维平面，而是能够在三维空间中展示和互动。这种技术为用户提供了更沉浸式的体验，拓展了网页设计的可能性，使得网站和应用程序可以更具互动性和立体感。JSAR工具使得开发者能够轻松实现这种空间渲染，为未来的Web设计开辟了新的方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某产品页面信息不足、缺乏示例和功能描述不清的反馈。

不同观点：
• vorgol：认为页面上的示例要么无法使用，要么缺失，建议在首页显著位置添加有效示例链接，以便用户更好地理解产品。

• andybak：对页面中使用如"空间"和"沉浸式"等词汇，预期该产品至少能在某些头戴设备上运行，暗示对当前产品描述和实际功能之间的落差感到困惑。

• vrighter：直接指出页面没有清晰说明产品到底是什么，虽然强调了兼容性，但缺乏对产品本身功能的介绍。

• JoeOfTexas：表示找不到任何产品功能的演示，质疑是自己没看到还是页面确实缺少示例。

补充讨论：
• 所有评论共同指向了页面信息不足的问题，特别是缺乏实际示例和产品核心功能的清晰说明。
• 争议焦点在于用户期望看到具体示例或演示来理解产品，但页面未能满足这一需求，导致用户困惑和不满。

data.title: Jobs data denialism won't fool anyone
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了特朗普否认就业数据的行为不会误导大众，并强调美国政府发布的经济数据通常是可靠且高质量的。文章指出，尽管数据在最初发布后可能会根据新信息进行修订，但这些修订都是经过详细记录和解释的。作者内特·西尔弗承认数据分析过程中存在人为错误和偏见，但认为通过严格的分析和建模，大多数情况下可以得出正确结论。他还提到，政府机构在快速提供信息和确保数据精确之间面临权衡，而试图否认或扭曲经济数据只会损害美国的经济领导地位，增加商业、工人和投资者的不确定性。文章最后建议，人们不应轻易质疑经济数据的可靠性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对就业数据和否认主义的问题讨论

不同观点：
• benbojangles的观点：对其他国家如何隐藏就业问题的方式感到好奇，认为可能存在一些具有创造性或幽默性的做法。他似乎对探讨就业数据操纵的问题抱有娱乐性和趣味性的期待。

• Nevermark的观点：
  ◦ 对特朗普否认就业数据的做法持批评态度，认为这种“数据否认主义”无法欺骗任何人，且无助于解决问题。
  ◦ 提出“沉没成本谬误选民”的概念，暗示有些选民因为已经投入支持某一方，即便面对明显的问题也选择忽视或继续支持。
  ◦ 指出错误信息的目标往往不是为了欺骗专家或知情者，而是为了影响那些信息不对称或不充分了解情况的公众。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于就业数据的真实性和政客对数据的操纵或否认。Nevermark批评了特朗普对就业数据的否认，认为这种做法具有误导性，而benbojangles则更关注其他国家可能采用的隐藏就业问题的方式，表现出对这一现象的娱乐化解读。
• Nevermark进一步分析了选民在面对错误信息时的心理状态，特别是“沉没成本谬误”如何影响选民的决策，这是一个更深层次的政治心理学讨论。
• 评论还提到了错误信息传播的策略，即它可能不是为了欺骗专家，而是为了影响那些信息获取不足的群体。

I’ve had a fun weekend
1
visiting family in Kansas City, but I figured this story was timely enough to be worth publishing on a Sunday. Also, time flies: It’s August, which means that it’s time for a new Subscriber Questions post, ideally this week unless further news intervenes. You can submit your questions in the comments to
SBSQ #22
.
Subscribe
If you’d asked me 20 years ago, when I made a living playing online poker and running projections for Baseball Prospectus, I would have told you that,
of course
, I’m a Data Guy. Treat the numbers with caution, because it’s easy to
build bad models
or otherwise screw up in umpteen ways when working with complex statistical data under deadline pressure. But at the end of the day, we all have to make decisions based on incomplete information. Businesses particularly face this problem: new hires or capital investments typically have a long time horizon. If you’re not going to make these choices based on your best estimate of the situation,
given the relevant uncertainties — well, what exactly
are
you going to base them on?
These days, I’d say my relationship with the Data Guy label has become more fraught. In one of my particular subfields, election forecasting, there’s been a lot of bad work, which probably did more to misinform the conversation than contribute to it. And more broadly, I do buy
to
some
extent
that “science has been politicized”. Sometimes I've seen the admonition “just trust the numbers” used as a blunt insturment to suppress legitimate dissent. Data is collected by and interpreted by humans, and human error and bias play a role at every step of the process.
The important thing is to be
right
, and probably 90 percent of the time, going through the rigor of kicking the tires on the data
2
and then explicitly modeling a situation helps you get there. But I’ll give a little more weight these days to the
mesoscale
rather than the micro. Having a good bullshit detector — heuristics honed by life experience — comes in handy that remaining 10 percent of the time.
When it comes to economic data produced by the United States government, however, people play that 10 percent “get out of jail free” card far too often. And usually, they’re the ones producing the bullshit, often to spin away politically inconvenient data.
Share
U.S. economic data is pretty reliable
I’ve worked a lot with data produced by the Bureau of Labor Statistics and other federal agencies. In fact, an economic index based on a half-dozen of these statistics is part of our presidential election forecast, so we’ve pulled this data all the way back to World War II.
3
And I consider it to be of very high quality. When BLS data is revised as more information becomes available, it’s meticulously
documented
and
explained
. For more on how this works, including just how difficult the BLS’s job is and how it’s being made harder by declining survey response rates and cuts to federal agencies that track economic activity, I’d strongly recommend this edition of the
Odd Lots
podcast with Bill Beach, the former BLS commissioner under Trump 1.0 and Biden. It might not be the most riveting interview, but one thing that comes through is just how much of a straight-shooter he is:
And yes, U.S. government economic data is revised — more for some data series than for others — because measuring something as complex as the modern American economy is an incredibly challenging task. Moreover, the BLS and other federal agencies are essentially trying to serve two purposes at once. On the one hand, they’re hoping to provide actionable information as fast as they reasonably can to employers, investors, job-seekers, policymakers and the Federal Reserve. On the other hand, they’re trying to formulate a “permanent record”, data that is treated as ground truth in future economic analysis. Those imply taking different positions in the unavoidable trade-off between speed and precision.
That doesn’t mean the BLS doesn’t face challenges like the ones that Beach outlined. A particular problem in recent reports seems to have been in
overestimating state and local educational jobs
, for instance.
And there’s also a more subtle factor at play. When data is published as part of the official record, there’s going to be a tendency to do things “by the book” in a way that establishes greater transparency or more consistency with past methods. Tyler Cowen
considers this a “bias”
of its own kind, and perhaps there’s something to that. Sometimes, whe

data.author: koolba
data.article_summary: 近期毕业生面临严峻的就业市场，许多人表示求职过程如同“黑洞”，投递数百份简历却鲜有回应，甚至在计算机科学和工程等高需求专业也是如此。以Jensen Kornfeind为例，他投递了70多份申请，只有三次面试，其中两次被无视。全国经济数据显示，毕业生失业率升至5.3%，远高于整体劳动力市场的4%。经济不确定性、特朗普的关税政策和联邦支出削减导致雇主招聘犹豫，而人工智能的兴起也取代了一些入门级岗位。Adam Mitchell拥有计算机科学学位和实习经验，但毕业后七个月内投递超过100份简历，仅获得两次面试和一份不适合的offer。科技行业裁员潮进一步加剧了就业困难，毕业生需更多耐心和努力寻求工作机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：当前科技行业就业市场的状况，尤其是对初级开发人员和高级开发人员的就业机会影响。

不同观点：
• Rover222认为，尽管过去两年对初级开发人员来说市场非常艰难，但有经验的开发人员仍然有需求，尤其是在AI浪潮推动下。他通过推荐和主动联系找到了工作机会，并感觉高级职位的市场相对较好。
• pvtmert指出，高期望和社交媒体带来的不现实标准导致一些人技能和工作质量下降，这使得AI更容易替代入门级职位。他还批评了年轻人因社交媒体影响而产生的不切实际期望。
• unencumberednut分享了个人经历，强调在就业市场困难时期可以通过其他工作自我提升，并鼓励毕业生享受这个过程，因为最终会找到工作。
• butterlettuce质疑那些曾经提倡"自力更生"的人现在是否也在失业队伍中。
• neom提到在南韩，大学毕业生找工作困难，AI和机器人技术的发展使得就业前景更加不明朗。
• anonzzzies的观察与大多数人相反，荷兰的应届毕业生似乎没有遇到就业问题，反而收到了很多工作机会。
• monster_truck描述了当前就业市场的极度困难，即使是高级职位也难以获得，并且感觉市场被某些不透明的力量操控。
• mcherm为刚毕业的儿子寻求建议，希望找到一份入门级的软件工程工作。
• jmpman质疑H1B签证对美国公民就业市场的影响，认为在本土毕业生就业困难时应减少H1B签证数量。
• code51预测，随着AI编码产品价格的调整，入门级职位可能会逐渐恢复，但恢复速度会很慢。
• Havoc对一些人抱怨高薪但无法负担房租表示困惑，认为年薪五万以上应该足够生活。
• tennisflyi和mixmastamyk都表示，入门级职位非常难找，很多公司甚至不提供反馈。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中存在争议的焦点包括AI和自动化对就业市场的影响，尤其是对初级职位的影响。
• 不同地区就业市场的差异，有些人观察到荷兰和美国的不同城市有不同的就业机会。
• 对社交媒体和高期望对年轻人就业心态的影响也有较多讨论。
• 还有对H1B签证政策的讨论，认为它可能影响了本土毕业生的就业机会。

Aug. 2, 2025, 6:00 AM EDT
By
Shannon Pettypiece
Recent graduates looking to enter an
increasingly shaky labor market
are painting a dire picture of their job search: “A black hole,” one said. “I’m disheartened,” said another. “I almost feel like it wasn’t worth going to school,” said a third.
NBC News asked people who recently finished technical school, college or graduate school how their job application process was going, and in more than 100 responses, the graduates described months spent searching for a job, hundreds of applications and zero responses from employers — even with degrees once thought to be in high demand, like computer science or engineering. Some said they struggled to get an hourly retail position or are making salaries well below what they had been expecting in fields they hadn’t planned to work in.
“It was very frustrating,” said Jensen Kornfeind, who graduated this spring from Temple University with a degree in international trade. “Out of 70-plus job applications, I had three job interviews, and out of those three, I got ghosted from two of them.”
The national economic data backs up their experience. The unemployment rate among recent graduates has been increasing this year to an average of 5.3%, compared to around 4% for the labor force as a whole, making it one of the toughest job markets for recent graduates since 2015, according to an analysis by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York released Friday.
“Recent college graduates are on the margin of the labor market, and so they’re the first to feel when the labor market slows and hiring slows,” said Jaison Abel, an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.
Across the economy, hiring in recent months has ground to its slowest pace since the start of the pandemic, with employers adding just 73,000 jobs in July, according to data released Friday. The number of longer-term unemployed people who have been out of work for more than 27 weeks increased last month by 179,000 to 1.8 million.
In short, it’s a pretty stable market for those who have a job, but a much more challenging one for those who are trying to get one, economists said.
Driving that trend is hesitation among employers to hire new workers amid wider economic uncertainty in the midst of President Donald Trump’s shifting tariff policies and federal spending cuts, economists have said. Then there is the emergence of AI, which some companies have said they are using to replace certain entry-level jobs, like those in customer support or basic software development.
“This is going to be an environment for recent college grads, as well as many workers, which is going to require more patience, more time and perhaps more diligence as they seek to attain employment,” said Mark Hamrick, a senior economic analyst for Bankrate.
Here is how several recent graduates described their job search:
Adam Mitchell
23
Atlanta
Bachelor’s degree, computer science
Unemployed
Adam Mitchell thought he was doing everything right. He majored in computer science at Georgia State University and interned at State Farm doing web development. He’d been told since he was a teenager that a degree in computer science was a guaranteed path to a high-paying job right out of college.
Adam Mitchell.
Courtesy of Adam Mitchell
“I was under the impression that since I’ve got three years of internship experience under my belt, this will be a cakewalk,” Mitchell said. “I was pretty quickly humbled. There’s nothing available.”
More than seven months after graduating, he’s applied for more than 100 jobs and gotten two interviews and only one job offer — for the 4 a.m. shift at Starbucks, which he didn’t take because the hours would make it too hard to pursue other opportunities. Among the jobs that turned him down: an hourly role at Costco and a customer service job in the call center at State Farm.
“The very few openings that there were would be so competitive that you would pretty much get a rejection notice as soon as you apply,” said Mitchell, who’s been living at home with his parents in the Atlanta area and spending down his savings.
“I can’t be doing this forever, just waiting for the dust to settle and things to kind of normalize again — I need a job,” said Mitchell, who worries about paying back his student loans.
Tech workers have been some of the hardest hit in a slowing job market, with more than 400 employers including Meta, Intel and Cisco announcing more than 130,000 jobs cut in 2025, according to
tech job site
TrueUp.
Those cuts mark a retrenchment after the hiring spree those companies went on after the pandemic, while an abundance of workers are vying for the remaining jobs, said Allison Shrivastava, an economist at Indeed Hiring Lab. Early adoption of AI is also likely driving some of the cuts and leading employers to rethink hiring plans in anticipation of AI’s future role, Shrivastava

data.title: One Dataset. No Warning. Google Took Everything. You're Not Safe Either
data.author: markatlarge
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了独立开发者Mark Russo在开发一款名为Punge的隐私保护应用时，因下载并解压一个用于研究的数据集，导致其Google账户被永久封禁。该数据集被误认为包含不当内容，但Google未提供具体解释或申诉途径。Mark失去了对其Gmail、Firebase、AdMob和Google Cloud等服务的访问权限，严重影响其应用开发和维护工作。尽管其应用仍在运行，但他无法推送更新或修复问题。Mark批评Google缺乏透明度和问责机制，呼吁建立更负责任和可申诉的内容管理系统。他希望通过分享自己的经历，引起公众对这一问题的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户与大型科技公司（如Google、Reddit等）在账户管理、内容审核和客户支持方面的矛盾与困扰

不同观点：
• 一些用户分享了他们与Google之间的负面经历，尤其是账户终止、债务处理和客户支持方面的问题。例如，[afandian]和[nicomt]都提到Google的支持过程像是卡夫卡式的噩梦，难以联系到真人支持，问题无法解决，最终导致他们决定"去Google化"。
• [benreesman]和[like_any_other]以讽刺和幽默的方式评论了这种情况，暗示用户应更谨慎地使用大型科技公司的服务，并暗示一些用户在问题发生前往往没有足够警惕。
• [Fade_Dance]对比了Google和Reddit的申诉流程，指出Reddit的体验甚至比Google更糟糕，用户每天浪费大量时间提交申诉表单，却往往没有反馈。
• [TheBozzCL]建议用户使用自己的域名关联电子邮件地址，以减少对单一服务提供商的依赖，增加账户恢复的可能性。
• [crossroadsguy]分享了自己早期使用Gmail被无故删除的经历，并通过个人经验提醒用户要备份选项和后备方案，同时批评了大型科技公司对用户权利的漠视。
• [RagnarD]直接指出，信任Google等科技公司处理重要事务是极其不明智的，建议避免使用其任何重要服务。

补充讨论：
• [nerdsniper]提到自己因上传的文件类型容易触发恶意软件检测，而选择加密上传，以防内容被误判。
• [_rm]对在Google Drive上存储NSFW内容的风险提出质疑，认为这并非无风险操作。
• [Havoc]对用户在Google云端硬盘存储大量成人内容被标记为CSAM（儿童性虐待材料）表示批评，认为这是不负责任的行为。
• [sidkris]和[isaacremuant]则分别提出了技术解决方案（如创建PWA）和对问题普遍性的认知，认为这些问题难以提前预见，直到用户亲自经历。

争议焦点：
• 用户在使用大型科技公司服务时面临的支持不力和账户管理问题，尤其是当问题涉及内容审核和债务处理时，用户往往感到无助和被忽视。
• 用户对是否应信任和依赖这些公司处理重要事务存在分歧，一部分人建议完全"去Google化"，另一部分人则认为可以通过技术手段和备份策略缓解风险。

44779797.article_content:
One Dataset. No Warning. Google Took Everything. You’re Not Safe Either.
Mark Russo
4 min read
·
1 day ago
--
Listen
Share
Zoom image will be displayed
I’m an independent developer who built
Punge
, an on-device NSFW image detection app. The idea was simple: give people tools to manage sensitive content on their own phones — not in the cloud, not handed over to big platforms, but fully under their control.
The inspiration was personal. I’d heard about a woman whose intimate photo was stolen and distributed by an ex. Her story stayed with me. I wanted to build something that could help people prevent that kind of violation. That’s where
Punge
came from — a privacy-first tool for personal safety.
To make the app effective, I trained a lightweight AI model and conducted a benchmark study comparing it to existing solutions, including Google Cloud Vision — the results of that benchmark are in
this article
.
To my surprise,
Punge
outperformed other available models, including Google’s own solution. I was excited by the results and wanted to expand my testing. So I visited
Academic Torrents
— an open platform for sharing research datasets, publications, and educational resources via the BitTorrent protocol, specifically designed for academic use.
There, I found a dataset commonly used in NSFW image classification research:
👉
https://academictorrents.com/details/1cda9427784a6b77809f657e772814dc766b69f5
I downloaded the dataset and unzipped it on my Google Drive.
Then, everything fell apart.
Google Suspended My Entire Account — Permanently
Shortly after running the file was unzipped, Google
suspended my account for a content policy violation
. I received no warning and no specific explanation other than it was a CSAM violation. Appeals were automatically denied, and I was never told what file triggered the flag.
Overnight, I lost access to:
Gmail
— 14 years of personal and professional history
Firebase
— my backend infrastructure
AdMob
— my monetization platform
Google Cloud
— all associated services and tools
This wasn’t just disruptive — it was
devastating
. I rely on these tools to develop, monitor, and maintain my apps. With no access, I’m flying blind.
If the dataset contained inappropriate or restricted material, I certainly never saw it or intended to interact with it. And if that’s the case, the dataset source — not a downstream developer — should be investigated and corrected. But Google has offered
no transparency
,
no accountability
, and
no way to respond or appeal to a human being
.
This Could Happen to Anyone
It’s not just developers at risk. Any researcher, content moderator, or regular user could unknowingly receive or process inappropriate material — whether through a meme, a dataset, or even spam — and lose their account in an instant. No warning. No investigation. Just erased.
I fully support systems that prevent harmful content. But a zero-tolerance policy without transparency or due process
hurts innocent people
— and there’s currently
no way to clear your name
or even understand what happened.
My Apps Are Still Live — But I Have No Control
What’s surreal is that my apps are still available in both app stores:
🟢
Punge for iOS
🤖
Punge for Android
\
They work — for now. But I have no way to:
Push updates for Android
Access analytics
Fix bugs
Monitor issues
Ensure they stay live
And to make it worse,
Google is still billing my credit card
for services attached to the suspended account — and I
have no way to reach them
. There is
literally no support channel
for suspended users. You’re just locked out and left to fend for yourself.
This Isn’t Just a Policy Failure — It’s a Warning
I was fully bought into the Google ecosystem, like millions of developers are. When Google suspended my account, they didn’t just remove access — they
cut off the oxygen
to everything I had built.
This isn’t about protecting users anymore. It’s about unchecked, opaque enforcement — and a total lack of accountability.
We need systems that:
Flag responsibly
Allow for investigation
Offer human review
Let innocent people reclaim their digital lives
What’s happening now is not responsible moderation. It’s a broken system — and it’s happening more often than you think.
Please Share This Story
If you made it this far, thank you. I hope you’ll consider sharing this story. Cases like mine are
deeply isolating
— and if something like this happens to someone else, they may be too embarrassed or overwhelmed to speak up.
As an individual, you feel powerless. Platforms are enormous; the process is opaque; the damage is personal and immediate.
If you’ve experienced something similar or have advice, legal resources, or media contacts, I’d truly love to hear from you.
We can’t fix what we don’t talk about.
Please connect with me on:
LinkedIn::
https://www.linkedin.com/in/mark-russo-60a46912/
TIkTok demo of punge:
https://www.tiktok.com/t/ZPHpvAsAoDwgm-f4wjA/

• 用户对是否应信任和依赖这些公司处理重要事务存在分歧，一部分人建议完全"去Google化"，另一部分人则认为可以通过技术手段和备份策略缓解风险。

data.title: Will data centers crash the economy?
data.author: muzz
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了美国当前AI数据中心建设的繁荣是否可能导致经济危机。尽管整体经济数据表现平平，AI技术快速发展带动了对计算能力（compute）的巨大需求，推高了相关公司的资本支出（capex）。微软、谷歌、Meta和亚马逊等大公司在数据中心上投入巨资，希望获得收入和利润，而苹果则选择不参与这场投资热潮。

文章指出，当前AI基础设施的支出已经超过互联网泡沫时期的电信和互联网基础设施支出，甚至对经济增长起到了类似私人部门刺激计划的作用。然而，作者也警告，历史上的铁路和电信泡沫最终都导致了经济崩溃，因为基础设施建设超前于需求增长。如果AI行业的收入无法跟上资本支出的增长速度，数据中心行业及大型科技公司可能会面临崩溃风险，进而影响整体经济。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对技术趋势的未来发展预期以及财务数据展示方式的讨论

不同观点：
• [techpineapple] 认为当前正处于技术炒作周期的上升阶段，虽然无法确定具体时间，但未来的变化可能会令人不快。他引用了“黎明前最黑暗”的比喻，暗示可能会有一个突然的转折点，或者暗示当前的状况可能会比预期更快地恶化。

• [MuffinFlavored] 对未根据通货膨胀调整的资金随时间变化的图表表示质疑，认为这种图表不太合理。他的观点侧重于财务数据的准确性和合理性，强调了通胀调整在长期数据分析中的重要性。

• [NoPicklez] 简短地表示不同意，直接否定了某种预期或可能性，但没有提供具体的论据或进一步解释。

补充讨论：
• [techpineapple] 的评论隐含了对技术趋势周期性变化的担忧，尤其是对可能出现的负面转折的预期，但没有明确具体是哪种技术或趋势。

• [MuffinFlavored] 的评论引发了对财务分析中数据展示方式的讨论，提出了通胀调整在分析中的必要性，这涉及到数据准确性和有效性的问题。

• [NoPicklez] 的简短评论虽然立场明确，但缺乏论据支持，可能反映了在快速讨论中的一种直观反应。

争议焦点：
• 技术趋势的发展预期存在不确定性，尤其是何时会出现转折点。
• 财务数据展示中是否需要通胀调整，这涉及到数据分析的准确性和合理性。

这些观点共同构成了对未来技术趋势和财务分析方法的不同预期和评价。

Photo via Amazon
The
U.S. economic data
for the last few months is looking decidedly meh. The
latest employment numbers
were so bad that Trump actually
fired the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics
, accusing her of manipulating the numbers to make him look bad. But there’s one huge bright spot amid the gloom: an incredible AI data center building boom.
AI technology is advancing fast, threatening (promising?) to upend many sectors of the economy. Nobody knows yet exactly who will profit from this boom, but one thing that’s certain is that it’s going to take a lot of computing power (or “compute”, as they say). AI models take a lot of compute to train, but nowadays they also take a lot of compute to do inference — i.e., to “think about” and answer each question you ask. Inference compute now
represents most of the cost
of running advanced AI models, and increases in inference compute are responsible for
many of the ongoing performance gains
. So compute needs are probably only going to grow as AI keeps getting better.
Whoever provides this compute is going to make a huge amount of revenue. Whether that means they’ll make a lot of
profit
is another question, but let’s table that for right now; you can’t make profit if you don’t make revenue. So right now, tech companies have the choice to either sit out of the boom entirely, or spend big and hope they can figure out how to make a profit.
Roughly speaking, Apple is
choosing the former
, while the big software companies — Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Amazon — are choosing the latter. These spending numbers are pretty incredible:
Source:
Chris Mims
For Microsoft and Meta, this capital expenditure is now more than a third of their
total sales
.
Here’s
Chris Mims of the WSJ
:
The Magnificent 7 tech firms have collectively spent a record $102.5 billion on capex in their most recent quarters, nearly all from
Meta
,
Alphabet
(Google),
Microsoft
and
Amazon
. (
Apple
,
Nvidia
and
Tesla
together contributed a mere $6.7 billion.)…
Investor and tech pundit Paul Kedrosky says that, as a percentage of gross domestic product, spending on AI infrastructure has already exceeded spending on telecom and internet infrastructure from the dot-com boom—and it’s still growing. He also argues that one explanation for the U.S. economy’s ongoing strength, despite tariffs, is that spending on IT infrastructure is so big that it’s acting as a sort of
private-sector stimulus program
…
Capex spending for AI
contributed more to growth
in the U.S. economy in the past two quarters than
all of consumer spending
, says Neil Dutta, head of economic research at Renaissance Macro Research, citing data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis. [emphasis mine]
Here’s that chart from Kedrosky, who has been
doing an excellent job
following this story as it unfolds:
Source:
Paul Kedrosky
Side note: I’m actually not sure Kedrosky is right about the height of the telecom boom. His chart shows the level of capex for 2020, when 5G and fiber infrastructure was being built out. But
Doms (2004)
shows U.S. telecom capex reaching $120 billion in 2000:
Source:
Doms (2004)
That would have been around 1.2% of U.S. GDP at the time — about where the data center boom is now. But the data center boom is still ramping up, and there’s no obvious reason to think 2025 is the peak, so Kedrosky’s point still stands.
I think it’s important to look at the telecom boom of the 1990s rather than the one in the 2010s, because the former led to
a gigantic crash
. The railroad boom
led to a gigantic crash too
, in 1873 (
before
the investment peak on Kedrosky’s chart). In both cases, companies built too much infrastructure, outrunning growth in demand for that infrastructure, and suffered a devastating bust as expectations reset and loans couldn’t be paid back.
In both cases, though, the big capex spenders weren’t
wrong
, they were just
early
. Eventually, we ended up using all of those railroads and all of those telecom fibers, and much more. This has led a lot of people
to speculate
that big investment bubbles might actually be
beneficial to the economy
, since manias leave behind a surplus of cheap infrastructure that can be used to power future technological advances and new business models.
But for anyone who gets caught up in the crash, the future benefits to society are of cold comfort. So
a lot of people are worrying
that there’s going to be a crash in the AI data center industry, and thus in Big Tech in general, if AI industry revenue
doesn’t grow fast enough
to keep up with the capex boom over the next few years.

data.title: A parser for TypeScript types, written in TypeScript types
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: "tsints" 是一个用 TypeScript 类型编写的 TypeScript 类型解析器，不包含任何 JavaScript 代码。它可以将 TypeScript 类型解析为类似 @babel/parser 生成的抽象语法树（AST）。项目提供了示例代码，展示如何使用 `Parse` 类型来解析特定字符串并生成相应的 AST。不过，由于其复杂的类型运算，每次运行 `tsc` 时可能会增加几秒的等待时间。项目目前有 17 个星标和一个分支，但尚未提供详细描述或发布任何版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TypeScript类型系统的复杂性及其应用

不同观点：
• **激励与挑战**：johnfn认为，看到有人完成了像解析TypeScript类型这样复杂的任务，能激励自己解决相对简单的问题。这种观点强调复杂类型系统的积极影响，认为它可以作为解决问题的动力。

• **具体应用展示**：drej通过分享一个视频链接，展示了TypeScript类型系统运行DOOM游戏的实例，进一步强调TypeScript类型的强大能力。

• **工具推荐**：mpoteat推荐了一个包含高阶构建块和类型解析器组合工具的网站（http://hkt.code.lol），为对类型系统感兴趣的人提供了实际操作资源。

• **理论支持**：maxloh提到TypeScript的类型系统是图灵完备的，并提供了一个相关链接以证明这一点，从理论上支持TypeScript的强大功能。

• **质疑实际用途**：nottorp质疑TypeScript类型系统的实际应用，特别是与C++的元编程能力相比，并提出是否可以在编译时通过TypeScript类型运行整个工资应用。

• **工具比较**：tmcanada询问TypeScript与TypeBox的比较，提出了另一种类型系统工具，希望了解其优劣。

• **批评与担忧**：phplovesong认为TypeScript的复杂性增加可能导致其走下坡路，怀念早期版本的简洁性，并指出其复杂性与OCaml等语言的复杂类型系统相似。

• **负面评论**：owebmaster用“cult”一词形容TypeScript，表达了对TypeScript日益复杂的不满或不屑。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个外部链接和工具，如展示TypeScript类型系统能力的视频、类型系统操作的在线资源（http://hkt.code.lol）以及TypeBox工具的链接。
• 争议的焦点主要集中在TypeScript类型系统的实际用途和复杂性上，部分人对其复杂性持批评态度，而其他人则展示了其强大的功能和应用潜力。

44781523.article_summary: "tsints" 是一个用 TypeScript 类型编写的 TypeScript 类型解析器，不包含任何 JavaScript 代码。它可以将 TypeScript 类型解析为类似 @babel/parser 生成的抽象语法树（AST）。项目提供了示例代码，展示如何使用 `Parse` 类型来解析特定字符串并生成相应的 AST。不过，由于其复杂的类型运算，每次运行 `tsc` 时可能会增加几秒的等待时间。项目目前有 17 个星标和一个分支，但尚未提供详细描述或发布任何版本。

data.title: Why doctors hate their computers (2018)
data.author: mitchbob
data.article_summary: 2015年5月，作者与其他外科医生在波士顿市中心参加为期16小时的强制性计算机培训，学习新上线的Epic医疗软件系统。该系统耗资16亿美元，旨在使医院技术现代化。尽管Epic在美国广泛应用，但其复杂性令医生们感到困扰，尤其是面对众多相似选项卡和功能时。尽管作者早期对技术适应良好，但随着系统全面实施，医生们发现其增加了工作负担，导致工作与生活失衡和职业倦怠。2016年一项研究显示，医生每看一小时病人，需花两小时处理计算机工作，这导致许多医生感到压力和抑郁。Epic本应提高效率，但实际上增加了医生的工作量，引发广泛不满。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子病历系统（EMR）及现代技术在医疗中的应用，包括其优缺点、对医生工作流程的影响以及与传统医疗方式的对比。

不同观点：
• 一些医生，如[cainxinth]的父亲，虽然不擅长使用现代技术，但通过努力适应，最终习惯了EMR系统。这表明年长医生在技术转型中的适应能力，即使初期存在困难。
• [jayd16]指出，医生使用的系统往往由非医疗人员采购，这些系统并不总能满足医生的实际需求，导致工作不便。例如，菜单中不相关的功能按钮影响了效率。
• [anon_cow1111]分享了一个关于医生缺乏基本计算机技能的个人经历，质疑即使经过长时间医学培训，一些医生在技术使用上的不足。
• [Abishek_Muthian]引用了医师Dr. Abraham Verghese的观点，批评现代医生过于依赖电子设备，而忽视了传统的体检方法，这可能影响医患关系和诊断质量。
• [BjoernKW]提到，医生通常只信任同行推荐的EMR系统，这导致即使有设计良好的系统，也难以推广，软件公司不得不雇佣医生作为销售。
• [johntfella]对纸质办公的消失感到遗憾，认为现代医疗系统虽然数字化，但失去了“家庭医生”的亲情感，且更容易被大型医疗机构控制。

补充讨论：
• [mitchbob]分享了一个参与式设计的例子，展示了某些医生如何主动改进EMR系统以提高其适用性。
• [Havoc]和[golem14]提到，现代技术系统（包括医疗和教育）往往过于复杂，用户界面不友好，导致使用不便。
• [dekhn]认为，一旦熟悉了EMR系统，医生和患者都能顺利操作，且现代系统使得记录转移更加方便，但对有严重健康问题的患者可能仍存在挑战。
• [russellpekala]提供了一个博客链接，讨论数据和AI在医疗和保险中的负面影响，指出系统性问题如生产力与工资不成比例增长（Baumol病）。
• [davnn]进一步探讨了医疗行业缺乏真正的竞争和创新动力，导致数字化投资不足。
• [zabzonk]则对现代影像技术在诊断中的应用表示赞赏，认为网络化医疗记录有助于快速获取信息。

• 技术在医疗中应用的利弊，尤其是EMR系统对医生工作效率和医患关系的影响。
• 年长医生对新技术的适应能力与技术系统设计的用户友好性之间的矛盾。
• 现代医疗数字化趋势与传统医疗方式之间的平衡与取舍。

On a sunny afternoon in May, 2015, I joined a dozen other surgeons at a downtown Boston office building to begin sixteen hours of mandatory computer training. We sat in three rows, each of us parked behind a desktop computer. In one month, our daily routines would come to depend upon mastery of Epic, the new medical software system on the screens in front of us. The upgrade from our home-built software would cost the hospital system where we worked, Partners HealthCare, a staggering $1.6 billion, but it aimed to keep us technologically up to date.
More than ninety per cent of American hospitals have been computerized during the past decade, and more than half of Americans have their health information in the Epic system. Seventy thousand employees of Partners HealthCare—spread across twelve hospitals and hundreds of clinics in New England—were going to have to adopt the new software. I was in the first wave of implementation, along with eighteen thousand other doctors, nurses, pharmacists, lab techs, administrators, and the like.
The surgeons at the training session ranged in age from thirty to seventy, I estimated—about sixty per cent male, and one hundred per cent irritated at having to be there instead of seeing patients. Our trainer looked younger than any of us, maybe a few years out of college, with an early-Justin Bieber wave cut, a blue button-down shirt, and chinos. Gazing out at his sullen audience, he seemed unperturbed. I learned during the next few sessions that each instructor had developed his or her own way of dealing with the hostile rabble. One was encouraging and parental, another unsmiling and efficient. Justin Bieber took the driver’s-ed approach: You don’t want to be here; I don’t want to be here; let’s just make the best of it.
I did fine with the initial exercises, like looking up patients’ names and emergency contacts. When it came to viewing test results, though, things got complicated. There was a column of thirteen tabs on the left side of my screen, crowded with nearly identical terms: “chart review,” “results review,” “review flowsheet.” We hadn’t even started learning how to enter information, and the fields revealed by each tab came with their own tools and nuances.
But I wasn’t worried. I’d spent my life absorbing changes in computer technology, and I knew that if I pushed through the learning curve I’d eventually be doing some pretty cool things. In 1978, when I was an eighth grader in Ohio, I built my own four-kilobyte computer from a mail-order kit, learned to program in
BASIC
, and was soon playing the arcade game Pong on our black-and-white television set. The next year, I got a an Apple II computer and eventually became the first kid in my school to turn in a computer-printed essay (and, shortly thereafter, the first to ask for an extension “because the computer ate my homework”). As my Epic training began, I expected my patience to be rewarded in the same way.
My hospital had, over the years, computerized many records and processes, but the new system would give us one platform for doing almost everything health professionals needed—recording and communicating our medical observations, sending prescriptions to a patient’s pharmacy, ordering tests and scans, viewing results, scheduling surgery, sending insurance bills. With Epic, paper lab-order slips, vital-signs charts, and hospital-ward records would disappear. We’d be greener, faster, better.
But three years later I’ve come to feel that a system that promised to increase my mastery over my work has, instead, increased my work’s mastery over me. I’m not the only one. A 2016 study found that physicians spent about two hours doing computer work for every hour spent face to face with a patient—whatever the brand of medical software. In the examination room, physicians devoted half of their patient time facing the screen to do electronic tasks. And these tasks were spilling over after hours. The University of Wisconsin found that the average workday for its family physicians had grown to eleven and a half hours. The result has been epidemic levels of burnout among clinicians. Forty per cent screen positive for depression, and seven per cent report suicidal thinking—almost double the rate of the general working population.
Something’s gone terribly wrong. Doctors are among the most technology-avid people in society; computerization has simplified tasks in many industries. Yet somehow we’ve reached a point where people in the medical profession actively, viscerally, volubly hate their computers.
On May 30, 2015, the Phase One Go-Live began. My hospital and clinics reduced the number of admissions and appointment slots for two weeks while the staff navigated the new system. data.title: Human speech may have a universal transmission rate (2019)
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人类语言传输信息的速率和效率，以及影响该速率的因素。

不同观点：
• Yenrabbit认为，"思考和传输"可能是信息交流的瓶颈，而非接收信息。他质疑如果不需要被所有人理解，是否可以提高发送和接收速率。
• brav8isgood讨论了语言之间的传输速率差异，引用法语和瑞士法语的对比，并提出非语言因素（如身体语言、语调）可能影响信息传输效率。
• nialv7对研究的小样本量（170人）和使用音节率作为信息代理的合理性提出质疑，认为结果不能过于认真对待。
• joshdavham以法语和日语为例，认为某些语言由于单个词的意义密度较低，需要以更快的速度说话以传达相同的信息量。
• CMay引用了研究论文，指出不同语言和个体之间的信息传输速率存在差异，但所有语言都趋向于一个最佳的传输速率范围，且阅读任务可能影响结果。
• dcow提出语言作为压缩工具的概念，质疑研究中"比特"计数是否反映了思想的实际压缩和传输效率，并以土耳其语为例说明某些语言可能具有更高的信息密度。
• golem14关注阅读速度的差异，并提出同步翻译员的大脑是否不同，以及他们如何处理两种语言的问题。
• Aldipower质疑词汇量少的人是否说话更快。
• amadeuspagel提问，限制信息传输的因素是说话者还是听众。
• imglorp建议手语可能具有与口语相似的比特率，基于手语翻译员在对话中传达相同信息量所需的时间。
• t_minus_40认为，信息传输的效率取决于人而非语言，平庸者与天才或青少年之间的交流效率不同。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了具体研究的链接和相关讨论，如chadcmulligan和ChrisArchitect引用的2019年讨论。
• 有人（如paulwilsondev）提到Adam建议不要以2倍速听录音，可能与信息接收效率相关。

争议焦点：
• 研究方法的有效性，尤其是样本量和音节率作为信息代理的合理性。
• 不同语言之间的传输速率差异及其影响因素，包括文化、非语言因素以及个体差异。
• 信息传输速率的限制因素是说话者还是听众。

主要讨论点：随机数生成中的技术选择及其优缺点，特别是关于位掩码方法和随机范围生成的无偏性问题。

不同观点：
• Stevan认为2021年的一篇博客文章中提到了一些较新的随机数生成技术，暗示可能有更先进的方法值得关注。
• Eru指出Python的CPython实现中使用了位掩码和拒绝采样的方法，但存在一个已知bug：当生成范围的大小是2的幂时，会出现较高的拒绝率。Eru进一步解释，这种最差情况应出现在范围大小为2*x+1时，但目前该bug未被修复，以保持随机数输出的稳定性。
• Zokier支持位掩码方法，认为其简单易懂且性能良好，对其他更复杂且 slower 的解决方案表示不解，并询问在实时固定延迟条件下，哪种方法是无偏的最佳选择。
• Dspillett分享了自己早年作为学生时的编程经历，通过手动洗牌来减少随机选择中的偏差，尽管这种方法效率不高，但在其特定应用中有效。他还回忆了自己早期编程时的学习经历，带有些许怀旧色彩。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了历史上的编程实践和个人经验，如Dspillett提到自己使用BASIC和6502汇编语言进行随机数偏差分析的经历，这为讨论增加了一些历史和技术背景。
• Cbarrick提供了一个存档链接，可能意在补充更多相关信息，但未详细说明其立场或观点。

争议焦点：
• 位掩码方法的优劣及其适用场景是讨论的焦点，特别是在效率和无偏性之间的权衡。Eru和Zokier对该方法的看法存在一定分歧，Eru指出了其存在的bug，而Zokier则强调其简单性和实用性。
• 不同应用场景下（如实时系统）对随机数生成技术的需求差异，也是讨论中的一个隐含争议点。

data.title: Poorest US workers hit hardest by slowing wage growth
data.author: hhs
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：低收入工人在经济政策中的处境以及工资与通胀之间的关系

不同观点：
• fluxkernel和yalogin认为，低收入工人在任何与金钱相关的经济变动中受到的打击最大，尤其是工资增长缓慢甚至停滞，最近的法案让情况更加恶化。yalogin特别指出，最贫困人群的工资长期未有实质增长，未能跟上通胀。
• thuridas和einrealist指出，针对富人的减税政策可能导致资金流入房地产市场，推高房价，反映了“涓滴经济学”的迷思，即富人受益的政策不会自动惠及穷人。
• jmpman和potato3732842讨论了房租对低收入工人的影响，jmpman认为房东会通过提高租金吸收最低工资的增长，而potato3732842则质疑先前认为通胀对穷人有利的观点如今为何不再流行。
• hellgas00和RickJWagner提供了另一种视角，认为尽管2022年工资增长较高，但当时的通胀也更高，如今通胀下降，低收入者的实际工资开始增长，文章未提及这一背景让人质疑其动机。

补充讨论：
• PeterStuer将问题归结为现代奴役制度，指出低收入工人被无权利的劳工替代，政策上只给予有限的救济。
• shmerl批评了官方数据的可靠性，暗示政府提供的数据可能经过操控，以呈现政府想要的版本。
• rr808对高收入群体的工资增长数据表示怀疑，质疑是否真有人获得了4.7%的加薪。
• user9999999999主张大幅提高最低工资至25美元/小时，认为这是对亿万富翁征税的一种方式。

争议焦点：
• 工资增长与通胀之间的关系以及如何解读相关数据。
• 针对富人的减税政策是否会间接损害低收入工人的利益，尤其是通过推高房价。
• 最低工资标准是否应该大幅提高以改善低收入者的生活状况。

data.title: Cube: Packing a 5x5x5 cube with Y-pentominoes
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种名为“25Y”或“125立方”的拼图游戏，包含13个由3个白色立方体和2个深色立方体组成的Y形五连方块，以及12个由2个白色立方体和3个深色立方体组成的Y形五连方块。目标是将这些部件装入一个5x5x5的立方盒中，形成类似国际象棋棋盘的图案。由于手动解决非常困难，作者编写了一个程序，将问题转化为布尔可满足性问题，并使用SAT求解器找到解决方案。已知有1264种装箱方法，考虑立方体对称性后。作者进一步发现，其中只有5种是“孤立”的解决方案，即无法通过交换相邻部件的“尖端”立方体得到其他方案。这些孤立方案通过计算机分析在一小时内确定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个看似简单的立体拼图问题及其可能的解决方案

不同观点：
• 3eb7988a1663认为这个问题看似简单，但实际尝试可能会非常困难。该评论者正考虑购买一套拼图亲自尝试，并提到目前看到的一些套件价格在40-50美元之间。他还提出一个疑问，即最终的解决方案是否要求所有面都是棋盘图案，并认为如果真是这样，可能会简化问题。

• 112233提出了一个更具体的问题，询问是否可以通过改变Y形五连块的形状来防止三种可交换的配置出现。这个评论关注的是拼图块的几何变形及其对解决方案的影响。

• dandanua则分享了对前几个解决方案的观察，指出前三个解决方案中，有一个侧面包含五个方向相同的拼图块，而最后一种解决方案中，虽然也有五个拼图块在同一侧，但其中一个块是翻转的。这表明评论者在分析不同解决方案之间的模式和差异。

补充讨论：
• 3eb7988a1663对拼图价格的关注表明市场价格在讨论中也是一个相关因素。
• 112233的提问引出了一个关于拼图块形状修改的潜在解决方案，这可能涉及到拼图设计的深层次问题。
• dandanua的观察提供了一个对现有解决方案的模式分析，可能对其他尝试解决该问题的人提供启示。

争议焦点：目前在这些评论中没有直接的争议，但3eb7988a1663对问题简化的假设与其他评论者对具体细节的关注形成对比，显示出对问题复杂性的不同理解。

44764261.article_content:
The "25Y" or "125 cube" puzzle
The puzzle is made of 13 of the Y-shaped pentomino consisting of 3 white cubes and 2 dark cubes and 12 Y-pentominoes of 2 withe cubes and 3 dark cubes. For this reason, the puzzle is called 25Y-puzzle sometimes.
The goal is to pack these pieces into a 5x5x5 box generating a checkerboard pattern.
The task of packing the pieces into the box is the really demanding part - if you have managed this the creation of the checkerboard is almost trivial and we will ignore this from here on.
Since I have never managed to find a solution by hand I wrote a program which is able to solve the problem.by transfroming it into a boolean satisfiability problem and let a SAT-solver do the rest of the job.
It is well known that there are 1264 possible ways to pack the box if the solutions are reduced by the 48 symmetries of the cube [
1
].
When my program started working and listed several solutions to the problem I observed that some solutions differed only by the position of two puzzle pieces. At first I thought that there was still something wrong with the program because I could not imagine how this could be possible.
But a closer examination revealed that in these cases just the "spike" of a piece - the cube which is not collinear with the other 4 cubes - exchanged between two adjacent pieces. This can only happen in a few different configurations:
spike swap
Let us now call a solution to the puzzle
isolated
, if it cannot be derived from another solution by a spike swap. Obviously, this is the case if and only if adjacent pieces in the puzzle never are in a configuration depicted above.
I wondered how many of the 1264 solutions are isolated solutions. The computer analysis with the SAT-solver showed in about 1 hour CPU-time that there are just 5 isolated solutions. They are depicted
here
.
[1] Chris Bouwkamp, The Cube-Y Problem,               Cubism For Fun                      25              (December 1990 - January 1991), part 3, pp. 30-43. (includes a listing of all 1264 solutions)
[2] C.J. Bouwkamp and D.A. Klarner, Packing a Box with Y-pentacubes,               Journal of Recreational Mathematics                      3              (1970), no. 1, pp. 10-26.

data.title: Camera Genealogica
data.author: JKCalhoun
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者通过一个装满旧照片的手提箱，意外地开始了一段家族影像的 genealogy（家谱学）之旅。作者的远房亲戚 Faye Coble 活到了103岁，去世后她的照片被遗留下来，最终传到了作者手中。作者对这些照片进行了数字化处理，约800张照片被扫描、修复并保存为数字副本，以防止原始照片因时间或意外而损坏。作者还通过云存储和分享给亲属来备份这些照片，并上传到 Ancestry.com 和 Find-A-Grave.com 等网站，以供更多人查看和保存。通过这种方式，作者不仅保存了家族历史，还 reconnect 了一位失散的亲属。文章强调了数字化保存家族照片的重要性，以及影像在 genealogy 研究中的独特价值。

44744801.article_content:
Engineers Need Art
Projects
SystemSix
Mooncraft 2000
Adam74
Stereographer
Camera Genealogica (Part 1)
30 Jul 2025
The suitcase of photos.
Faye Coble lived for 103 years. A happy accident that she was born in 1898 — that meant that she technically lived in three centuries.
She was the first daughter born to Gertrude Coble (née Harper) on a farm not far outside Kansas City, Missouri. Unfortunately, Faye was
quite young when her father died in a Kansas City hotel from gas asphyxiation. (Ironically, the hotel would be one of the first in Kansas
City to get electric lighting — too late though for Robert Coble.)
Gertrude would marry again (a
Calhoun
) and it is from that second marriage that my own grandfather would be born. Faye was my grandfather’s
half-sister.
Faye too would eventually marry. As I said at the start Faye lived a very long time but she would never have children. And so when Faye
died in 2001 somehow all of her photos and photo albums ended up ultimately in a suitcase that followed one of my grandfather’s daughters
from the midwest to a trailer in Eloy, Arizona. And there the photos sat under a spare bed until I showed up one day in 2015 to visit her,
my Aunt Mary.
I’m very much into genealogy. I think though after this suitcase was graciously passed along to me I came to realize that my interest
was more specifically as a kind of “photograph genealogist”. I found that I was little interested in taking the family tree back to
when we came across the Atlantic to settle in North America. I saw very quickly that the lives of my ancestors, as captured in the
photos, was what appealed to me. I think it goes without saying that a face, a pose in a photograph speaks more loudly about that person
and their life than a scribble in a church record about a Baptism performed in 1783 (for example). And I think I wanted to know who they were
(to the degree anyone can of course).
The Studio
It is very important to me to digitize old family photos and soon enough I would begin to scan in what turned out to be about 800 photos.
Further, I would try to identify who was in the photos, determine approximate dates for the photos, put them in something of a
chronological order. I spent perhaps a year or so on that first pass through the photos.
Why digitize the photos? The answer is probably obvious. It does no harm to the original and captures or preserves the photo in its
current state. Time may continue to ravage the photo but the digital version will remain unchanged in the coming decades.
Further, we can digitally restore the digital copy without touching the original photo in any way. In fact, we can digitally restore a
copy of the scanned image — leaving a “virgin” copy of the digital file unmolested. Apple’s Photos app always keeps a reference to the
original file — applying your edits on top of it but always having the means to get back the original scan.
In more than a few cases I believe I have even restored old photos to a state
better
than the original. Specks and dirt that
were on the negative (and so also in the original print) were removed — the overall image levels often balanced better than the original
prints as well.
It’s a sad fact too that as the family tree adds branches, family photo collections and photo albums either get broken up across the
children or perhaps go to only one of the offspring. In time they may disappear altogether — lost in a flooded basement or perhaps an
estate sale eventually lands them in a basket of random old photos in an antique store. Digital copies cost nothing and can be sent far
and wide via email to all interested relatives. And I have done that.
And of course since a digital copy can be stored in “the cloud” we no longer need fear fire, flood or theft of our family photo collections.
But I don’t just trust cloud services — I also have hard drive backups of all my photos should the cloud go away someday. And as I say,
I have also passed along copies to relatives who might also serve as some kind of back up.
And then there are sites like
Ancestry.com
and
Find-A-Grave.com
where you can upload photos for relatives or as a “memorial”. I have uploaded everything I have for the appropriate relatives online.
Find-A-Grave has a limit of twelve photos so I have chosen only the best of the best for that site.
How long will these sites be around? Who knows. But I suspect either way that all these photos will count as “assets” for the site and would
be something of a prize for perhaps a future site that might want to be reborn out of the ashes.
And as it happens I have come back in contact with an otherwise lost relative by way of having posted photos to Find-A-Grave of a relative
that we had in common. “How did you get all those photos of my husband’s mother?” read the first message I got from her. Later a photo exchange
netted an excellent photo of Faye no one on my side of the family had ever seen.
I may touch on other interesting things I found on my journey, but in this
44744801.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者通过一个装满旧照片的手提箱，意外地开始了一段家族影像的 genealogy（家谱学）之旅。作者的远房亲戚 Faye Coble 活到了103岁，去世后她的照片被遗留下来，最终传到了作者手中。作者对这些照片进行了数字化处理，约800张照片被扫描、修复并保存为数字副本，以防止原始照片因时间或意外而损坏。作者还通过云存储和分享给亲属来备份这些照片，并上传到 Ancestry.com 和 Find-A-Grave.com 等网站，以供更多人查看和保存。通过这种方式，作者不仅保存了家族历史，还 reconnect 了一位失散的亲属。文章强调了数字化保存家族照片的重要性，以及影像在 genealogy 研究中的独特价值。

Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
On July 25th, the UK became one of the first countries to widely implement age verification. Its Online Safety Act requires sites hosting porn and other content deemed “harmful” — including Reddit, Discord, Grindr, X, and Bluesky — to verify that users are over the age of 18. The early results have been chaotic. While many services have complied, some have pulled out of the country rather than face the risk and expense. Users have tricked the verification tools or bypassed them with VPNs. It’s just a taste of the issues that many other countries might face as they launch their own systems, and it’s a situation that privacy and security experts have long warned about — to little avail.
Following a yearslong political push to make the internet safer for kids, age verification has started seeping into online spaces across the globe. Lawmakers in the US, Europe, Australia, and elsewhere have all passed age-gating rules, and platforms have begun to comply. The likely methods for verification are similar to those in the UK. Platforms typically ask users to either enter a payment card, upload a government-issued ID, take a selfie, or allow a platform to use their data (like account creation dates and user connections) to “estimate” their age. Most rely on third-party services:
Bluesky
uses the Epic Games-owned Kids Web Services;
Reddit is working with Persona;
and Discord
has partnered with k-ID
.
The outcome so far is an assortment of online services handling sensitive user information — a “privacy nightmare,” says Cody Venzke, senior policy counsel at the American Civil Liberties Union. “There is no standardization of how age verification is supposed to take place.”
Some age verification platforms promise to erase your data after a certain period of time, like the seven days that Persona says it will keep the information used to verify your age on Reddit. But there’s no guarantee every service will do this, and there are still massive security risks given
how common
data breaches have become. Last year, a security researcher found that AU10TIX — an identity verification solution used by TikTok, Uber, and X — left user information and driver’s license photos exposed for months,
404 Media
reported
.
Governments are plowing toward the future of an age-gated internet
“When uploading your ID ... you are handing it over to a third party,” Venzke says. “You’re going to take their word that they’re going to delete it or remove it after they’re done using it.”
Despite these potential pitfalls, governments are plowing toward the future of an age-gated internet anyway. In addition to a crackdown in the UK, the European Union is hurdling toward a broad rollout of digital IDs,
Australia is age-gating search engines
, and users in many US states need IDs to access porn sites.
Age verification was long viewed as unconstitutional in the US, but the Supreme Court overturned that precedent
earlier in 2025
, concluding “adults have no First Amendment right to avoid age verification” if it’s meant to protect underage users from “obscene” content. Several states, including Alabama, Idaho, Indiana, Kentucky, North Carolina, and Texas, have implemented laws requiring verification measures on adult websites. Some have tried to extend this to social media or app stores as a whole, but so far, they’ve failed — lawsuits filed by NetChoice, a technology trade group backed by Google, Meta, X, Amazon, Discord, and other tech giants, have successfully blocked bills in
California
,
Arkansas
,
Georgia
,
Ohio
, and
Florida
.
As in the UK, there’s no guarantee against privacy and security breaches for states with age verification laws, and there’s little standardization in this bevy of rules. Efforts in the US also coincide with
escalating government digital surveillance
and
attempts to declare
expressions of LGBTQ sexuality, like drag shows, as obscene, raising the risks of handing over personal data even further.

主要讨论点：不同教学方法的有效性及其实施，特别是在音乐、阅读和编程教育中的应用。

不同观点：
• **音乐教学法（hyperman1）**：
   - 支持理解实际规则和正确术语，反对仅依赖“情境感知”的教学方法。
   - 个人经历显示，老师强调“情境感知”而不解释实际规则，导致困惑和不信任。

• **阅读教学法（giardini, twotwotwo, camgunz, jvvw, xg15）**：
   - **支持语音教学法（giardini, twotwotwo, jvvw）**：
     - 语音教学法被认为是有效的，可以帮助孩子成为优秀的读者。
     - twotwotwo分享了使用《Teach Your Child to Read in 100 Easy Lessons》的成功经验。
   - **质疑语音教学法的长期效果（camgunz, xg15）**：
     - camgunz引用英国的经验，指出语音教学法在长期效果上并不理想。
     - xg15指出语音教学法在某些情况下（如区分“house”和“horse”）可能不够有效。

• **编程教学法（bschne）**：
   - 强调基础理解的重要性，指出在编程教学中，学生需要对代码结构有低层次的理解，而不仅仅是解决问题。

• **教育系统的商业化（bluesounddirect）**：
   - 批评教育行业和教师将服务商业化，关注盈利而非学生的最佳利益。

补充讨论：
• **公共广播资金问题（ipython）**：
   - 提醒大家关注公共广播公司资金被削减的问题，指出该资金对新闻报道的支持。

• **个人经历（bsenftner）**：
   - 分享个人通过阅读漫画自学阅读的经历，强调早期阅读经验的重要性。

• **推荐资源（bwanab, zahirbmirza）**：
   - bwanab推荐了一个关于当前美国阅读项目问题的播客。
   - zahirbmirza分享了一篇支持语音教学法的文章。

争议焦点：
• 语音教学法是否为最有效的阅读教学方法。
• 是否应强调对规则和术语的基础理解，而非仅依赖情境感知。
• 教育系统的商业化对学生学习效果的影响。

44781469.article_content:
Aug 3, 2025
The Best Advice I Got at PagerDuty
I joined PagerDuty in 2011, back when the entire company could split a large pizza and still have leftovers. I left more than seven years later, as we were preparing to go public. Now, almost 7 years in the rearview mirror I’m dumbfounded by how much I didn’t know when we started.  I learned a lot by doing, and more than a little from my own mistakes but I also got a lot of advice. Here are some of my favourite pieces of advice I got personally:
“Yup, it’s tough.”
I don’t even remember the specific problem I was working on when I got this one. I’d like to think I was grinding through something tricky, but the truth is I’d probably drifted from problem-solving into whining. The actionable advice was just three words:
“Yup, it’s tough.”
That was the advice. Some things are hard. That doesn’t make them optional. You still have to solve them.
“Sometimes it’s you.”
We’ve all been in that meeting where a problem is sitting in the middle of the table, and everyone is politely waiting for someone else to pick it up. Early in your career, you don’t feel like it’s your turn yet. You assume someone more senior, more official, more
something
will step in. But sometimes, whether you realize it or not, they’re waiting for
you
. If you’re in the room, you’re a candidate for solving it.
“Keep track of your bank accounts.”
This one took a while to sink in with me. Every time you help someone out think of that as a deposit. Every time you need something from someone, consider that a withdrawal. The trick is to never let your balance go negative. This doesn’t apply to everyone but the people who keep score usually aren’t the ones who say so out loud. There are two sides to this one though, the advice-giver meant it from the perspective of getting things from people but it also struck me as a good description of who I don’t want to be. I try to find a way to help every new employee, just in case they are looking around fretting at starting with an empty bank account.
“Time to first referral.”
I think I had just given an offer for a PM that was turned down, we were talking about when you could be confident you’ve landed a candidate: was it the verbal? the signed contract? butt in seat?
The best answer
“When they refer someone.”
That might be a stretch as a hard metric, but I loved the clarity of it. It moves the goalpost from “they joined” to “they believe in us.” It’s something you can track and aim for,
“Slow down. Simplify. Repeat. Repeat again.”
This one came to me in every possible flavour. “Focus the message.” “Say it again.” “Say less, but clearer.” I needed it more than most, but most people need it more than they think. It’s easy to confuse “heard” with “understood” (Or even “was facing you while you said it” with “heard it.”)
Whatever idea you’re trying to communicate,your audience will absorb less than you think. And if it’s important, once is never enough. Clarity is a function of what got absorbed, not what got emitted.
“Show me.”
A great idea doesn’t count until it exists. I pitched some can’t-lose idea to a new executive. Their response?
“Show me.”
That was the bar. Not the pitch — the thing. Show the MVP. Show the signal. Show that the idea has legs. If you can’t demo it, maybe it’s not real yet.
“Be coachable.”
Everyone says they want feedback but far fewer people take it. The thing I didn’t appreciate early on: most people
want
you to succeed. They like helping. They’ve been through things you haven’t yet. Some of the advice will be wrong — but if you ignore it all, you’ll miss the part that could’ve saved you six months. Stay open. Everyone knows something you don’t. The best people aren’t just smart — they’re coachable.

data.title: HTML-in-Canvas
data.author: dannyobrien
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了WICG提出的新HTML Canvas API提案，旨在将HTML内容渲染到Canvas 2D和WebGL中。当前的`<canvas>`缺乏对复杂文本和内容渲染的支持，导致可访问性、国际化、性能和质量问题。该提案包括`layoutsubtree`、`drawElement`、`texElement2D`和`setHitTestRegions`等新方法，用于在Canvas中布局和渲染HTML元素，并改进可访问性和事件处理。渲染后的Canvas图像是静态的，后续元素变化不会自动更新。该提案还讨论了可访问性问题，并排除了对Offscreen Canvas和分离Canvas的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在网页中使用HTML和Canvas的结合，特别是将HTML渲染到Canvas中的提议及其技术实现和潜在问题。

不同观点：
• **支持该提议**：  
   - **samwillis**：认为在Canvas中增加字体和文本指标API将为网页应用开发带来好处，尤其是对于复杂文本布局（如分页富文本编辑）的实现非常有用。现有平台的文本处理能力有限，扩展Canvas的能力将解决这些问题。
   - **reactordev**：支持该提议，认为在某些场景下，重用HTML元素并直接在Canvas中渲染能避免一些以前的复杂解决方案（如html2canvas）。
   - **hyperhello**：认为可靠的富文本编辑更为重要，支持改进文本布局功能。

• **反对或质疑该提议**：  
   - **ha1zum**：认为HTML在Canvas中的使用感觉“被诅咒”，建议Canvas应作为独立的第一类格式，而不是嵌入HTML中。
   - **BobbyTables2**、**ttoinou**：以讽刺的方式表达对复杂嵌套（如HTML嵌套Canvas再嵌套HTML）的担忧，认为这种做法会导致技术堆栈过于复杂。
   - **mircerlancerous**：认为Canvas应该用于渲染HTML无法实现的效果，而不是替代DOM，当前的HTML渲染已经足够。
   - **pbohun**：认为Canvas的初衷是摆脱HTML和CSS的复杂性，主张开发新的简单UI库，而不是在Canvas中嵌入HTML。

• **技术实现与工具讨论**：  
   - **tombh**：提到SVG的`foreignObject`已经部分实现了该提案的功能，并提供了相关项目（如Snapdom）作为例子。
   - **c-smile**：介绍了Sciter框架中通过DOM元素生成图像的两种方式，认为这种方法可以解决类似问题。
   - **wg0**：建议开发一个简单的API，用于给定DOM元素并截取其子树的图像，目前缺乏此类工具。

• **安全与隐私担忧**：  
   - **mmastrac**：提到该提案可能带来的指纹识别风险，尽管具体细节尚未展开。

补充讨论：
• **性能与实现难度**：  
   - **talkingtab**：提到在Canvas中实现复杂的文本布局（如MDX文件）非常困难，现有的解决方案（如SDF、Troika等）效果不佳。同时，探讨了为何当前仍以HTML为首要开发平台的问题。
   - **SeanAnderson**：起初反对该提议，认为引入HTML到Canvas的复杂性过高，但后来承认在缺乏布局引擎的情况下，该提议也有其合理性。

争议焦点：
• 是否应在Canvas中直接支持HTML渲染，支持者认为这将带来更多功能和灵活性，反对者则担心复杂性和技术堆栈问题。
• Canvas的使用目的：是用于补充HTML的不足，还是完全替代HTML以摆脱其复杂性。
